name: Ried im Zillertal
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village in the Zillertal with a pilgrimage church and traditional customs.
beschreibung:
Ried im Zillertal extends at an elevation of 630 meters in the Zillertal, Achensee and the Tuxer Alpen and is a quiet village community. The village has around 1,300 inhabitants and stretches over a spacious area with typical Tiroler farmhouses and agricultural businesses.

Hikers get their money's worth on numerous marked trails around the village, and culturally interested visitors discover historic buildings and traditional customs, while families appreciate the diverse range of leisure activities and child-friendly accommodations. In the summer months (from May to October), the surroundings transform into an outdoor paradise.

Ried im Zillertal is especially suitable for families and those seeking relaxation who want to combine tranquility with activities. The good transport connections and proximity to larger towns make the stay particularly pleasant.
text:
Überblick

Ried im Zillertal is situated in the front-to-middle Zillertal valley within the Schwaz district at an altitude of 573 metres on the western bank of the Ziller River, home to around 1,370 residents. The municipality extends over the gently rising alluvial cone of the Riedbach stream and encompasses the hamlets of Großried, Kleinried, Taxach, and the sunny hillside farmsteads of Riedberg. Nestled against the slopes of the Tux Prealps, Ried captures abundant sunshine and sweeping views across the valley. It maintains a peaceful, authentic rural ambience while providing seamless access to the premier hiking trails and ski arenas of the Zillertal.

Geschichte

Ried was first documented around 1150, its name deriving from Middle High German words designating cleared woodland. The demanding labour of clearing forest land is reflected in the municipal coat of arms, which displays three severed white hands against a gold field, also commemorating the traditional glove-making craft that flourished in the valley during the 17th and 18th centuries. For generations, torrential mudslides from the Riedbach stream shaped the settlement, prompting extensive alpine flood defense works. The Late Baroque parish church of St. John the Baptist in Kleinried was erected between 1773 and 1779 to plans by Schwaz master builder Franz Singer. The church features an elegant spire, rococo stucco work, and a preserved pneumatic organ built by Anton Mayer in 1912.

Anreise

Travelling to Ried im Zillertal is effortless. Motorists exit the Inntalautobahn A12 at Wiesing/Zillertal and proceed southward along the B169 Zillertalstraße for about 15 kilometres directly to the Ried turnoff. Train travellers transfer at Jenbach main station onto the Zillertalbahn railway. Trains operate on a regular half-hourly schedule, stopping at the Ried im Zillertal halt within easy walking distance of the village centre. Free winter ski buses and VVT regional services connect the community to neighboring mountain cableways.

Tipps

A premier scenic experience is the Zillertaler Höhenstraße alpine road, featuring its northern access ramp ascending via Riedberg. The panoramic route climbs above 2,000 metres, presenting breathtaking vistas over the glaciated peaks of the High Zillertal Alps. Walkers can explore the dramatic Riedbach Gorge with cascading waterfalls or take gentle family bike rides along the flat Zillertal-Radweg cycle path beside the river. In winter, guests reach the Hochzillertal-Kaltenbach ski resort in mere minutes, enjoying ski-in possibilities near the village edge in favorable snow conditions. Nearby in Fügen, the Erlebnistherme Zillertal thermal spa provides soothing relaxation.
